scope: Analytic torus/torus surface-surface intersection in the coaxial configuration (twelfth and last canonical-primitive analytic SS slice, one cell): native intersect_torus_torus in crates/brep-core/src/intersections/torus_torus.rs, bridge op brep_intersect_torus_torus, typed TS adapter intersectTorusTorus. The cell reuses the existing recognizer and lift helpers unchanged (plane_torus::recognize_torus for both operands — the exact sixteen-patch strict ring-torus solid with tensor-product weights [[1,w,1],[w,w^2,w],[1,w,1]], w = cos(pi/4), R - r >= 1e-5, rigid affine placements admitted; plane_torus::lift_parallel and torus_residual; sphere_sphere::circle_curve and the exact rational 90-degree-arc parameter map). Coaxiality is certified, never forced: a pure-rounding axis tilt (64 binary64 epsilons plus the recognition-error angular allowances of both tori) or center-line offset (64 epsilons of the axial/radius terms plus both recognition deviations) snaps to coaxial, a recognition-scale tilt or offset (1e-9) reports near_coincidence, and a clearly tilted or off-axis pair is unsupported_surface (the general torus/torus pair is a quartic, out of scope — no numerical fallback). Either axis orientation is admitted (the torus surface is symmetric about its center plane, so the axis sign is irrelevant to the section and enters only the second torus's profile-angle map). Both surfaces are surfaces of revolution about the shared axis, so the section reduces to circle/circle in the meridian half-plane (rho >= 0, z along the first torus's axis): (rho - R_1)^2 + z^2 = r_1^2 against (rho - R_2)^2 + (z - h)^2 = r_2^2 with h the axial offset of the second center plane — the same closed form as sphere_torus (a = (d^2 + r_1^2 - r_2^2)/(2d), l^2 = r_1^2 - a^2, d the meridian center distance between (R_1, 0) and (R_2, h)): two distinct roots revolve into two exact circles (radius rho*, height z*, sorted by height then radius), the double-root tangencies (external d == r_1+r_2, internal d == |r_1-r_2|) stay tangency_or_multiple_root, the rho* collapse guard is the pole degeneracy (structurally unreachable for strict ring tori), equal meridian circles within the bands report coincident_trim, and provably separate or contained meridian circles resolve empty by the outward interval signs. Resolved contacts are exact rational circles (four 90-degree arcs, weights cos(pi/4)) with UV lifts on BOTH tori: iso-v parallels at the exact profile angle phi = atan2(z*, rho* - R) through the exact rational 90-degree-arc parameter map t = s/(1+s), s = sqrt(2) tan(phi/2)/(1 - tan(phi/2)), one degree-1 line per revolution quadrant patch of the profile row on both 4x4 tilings (the second torus's profile angle measured in its own frame, anti-parallel axes admitted).

limitations: Canonical operands only: both tori are the exact canonical strict ring-torus solid (R - r >= 1e-5; horn and spindle tori are refused at construction); everything else is an explicit unsupported_surface region, never a numerical fallback

Coaxial configuration only (either axis orientation): the two axes must be certified parallel and coincident; clearly tilted or off-axis pairs are honest unsupported_surface regions (the general torus/torus pair is a quartic) with a near_coincidence band at recognition scale, never forced coaxial

Resolved sections are the two-circle family only: two distinct meridian roots revolve into two exact circles; a one-circle resolved configuration is structurally unreachable for a strict ring-torus pair (every meridian root keeps rho* >= R - r >= 1e-5, far beyond the band) and is documented honestly rather than tested

The meridian tangencies (double roots, external d == r_1+r_2 or internal d == |r_1-r_2|) and the pole-collapse guard (rho* within the band — structurally unreachable for a strict ring torus) stay tangency_or_multiple_root — tangent contacts are never guessed circles; the pole guard is documented honestly rather than tested
Equal meridian circles (R_1 == R_2, h == 0, r_1 == r_2 within the bands) report coincident_trim — coincident surfaces are never guessed curves

NumericallyResolved is not certified complete-domain coverage and permitsTopologyChange stays false; consuming these sections in Booleans, tangency certification, the non-axial quartic configurations (Villarceau circles among them) and the general NURBS SS research spike stay open
